issues.legal_issue: After a decree has been executed and possession delivered, the appellate court cannot use its inherent powers to require the decree-holder to provide security or to restrain dealings with the property pending appeal when no protective direction was sought before execution.
material_facts: An appeal from a decree was pending when the decree-holders obtained possession of the disputed property through execution.
The appellants had not sought a stay of execution or other protective directions when execution was sought.

After possession had been delivered, the appellants applied for security for restoration of possession and mesne profits if they succeeded on appeal, and for an order restraining transfer of or creation of a charge over the property.
issues.conclusion: The requested security and restraint orders could not be granted after execution and delivery of possession. The application was rejected as to those requests.
issues.legal_principle: Order XLV, rule 13(1) of the Code of Civil Procedure provides for unconditional execution unless the court directs otherwise; rule 13(2) permits protective directions, including security, in connection with whether execution should be allowed or stayed, and rule 14 concerns increasing security already furnished. These provisions do not authorize a fresh security direction after unconditional execution has been completed. Order XX, rule 1 of the Supreme Court Rules allows a stay of execution but does not provide a separate power to direct the terms of completed execution; Order XLV, rule 5 preserves inherent powers, but they are not exercised where the Code sufficiently regulates the matter and the applicant failed to seek protection at the proper time. The court considered Mst. Jariutool-Butool v. Mst. Hoseinee Begum, Narayanan Chetti v. Arunachallam Chetti, and Khushaldas Gokuldas v. Chimanlal Kalidas, but found the cited historical regulations did not support the requested post-execution orders. Transfers during litigation remain subject to the law of lis pendens, and any recoverable mesne profits remain governed by law.

rule.if: appeal_from_decree_pending and decree_executed and decree_holder_in_possession and no_protective_order_sought_before_execution and post_execution_security_or_transfer_restraint_sought

predicates.appeal_from_decree_pending: An appellant has an appeal from a decree pending while seeking protection concerning the decree or its execution.
predicates.decree_executed: The decree has been executed before the requested protective order is sought.
predicates.decree_holder_in_possession: The decree-holder obtained possession of the property through execution of the decree.
predicates.no_protective_order_sought_before_execut: The appellant did not seek a stay or protective direction before execution was completed.
predicates.post_execution_security_or_transfer_rest: After execution, the appellant seeks security from the decree-holder or a restraint on dealings with the property pending appeal.
The court cannot grant the requested security or restraint through its inherent powers after execution and delivery of possession.

issues.definition: When an appeal from a decree is pending, the decree has been executed and possession delivered, no protection was sought before execution, and security or a restraint is sought afterward, the requested post-execution security or restraint is unavailable.
